oni.desc: The Oceanic Niño Index — 3-month running mean of Niño 3.4 SST anomalies, the official ENSO yardstick. +0.5°C sustained = El Niño; +2.0°C = very strong.
oni.inference: The ONI has cleared the El Niño threshold and is climbing toward very-strong territory on a trajectory that now clearly resembles 1997 and 2015. The official 3-month mean sits at +1.39°C for May–July and rising; because it lags the weekly Niño 3.4 (already +2.6°C by early August), the official index will keep climbing mechanically over the coming seasons even absent further surface warming. The 2023-style peak-and-fade the spring flagged as the downside case is off the table — this is a sustained, intensifying event.

roni.desc: The Relative ONI strips out the long-term warming baseline by comparing Niño 3.4 to the rest of the tropics. NOAA made RONI its primary ENSO index in February 2026; in a warmer mean ocean it runs below ONI, so it is the more honest strength gauge.
roni.inference: The ONI–RONI gap persists near 0.3–0.4°C — the warming-baseline signature — and this is the crux of the record question. On absolute ONI, +2.6°C weekly readings put 2026 past the 2015–16 record (+2.6°C peak) in reach. On RONI, which nets out the tropical ocean's own warming, the bar is higher — yet NOAA's August outlook still puts a 69% chance the OND RONI clears +2.5°C, which would exceed every event since 1950. Both indices sit firmly positive and rising together, confirming a genuine strengthening signal rather than a baseline artefact; on the more honest gauge, a new record is now the base case rather than the tail.

nino34.desc: Niño 3.4 weekly SST anomaly — the fastest-moving surface signal. It has now crossed the +2.0°C very-strong threshold.
nino34.inference: This is the chart that settled the debate. Niño 3.4 has climbed from +0.5°C in late May to +1.7°C in June to +2.1°C in mid-July to +2.6°C by early August — well across the +2.0°C very-strong line months before the seasonal peak. CFSv2 and ECMWF ensembles project the peak beyond +3°C, which would rank among the largest events ever recorded. The pace of the climb is itself historic; the only open question is how much higher it goes before the autumn–winter maximum.

subsurface.desc: Warm Water Volume anomaly — the subsurface heat reservoir fuelling surface warming. A downwelling Kelvin wave carried anomalies up to +10°C at depth east across the Pacific.
subsurface.inference: The subsurface reservoir remains exceptionally deep and is feeding the surface exactly as an intensifying event requires. NOAA's August discussion cites subsurface anomalies reaching +10°C at depth — deeper than the +8°C carried by the earlier Kelvin wave — running warmer than the 1997–98 event at the same calendar stage. Crucially, unlike 2014, the heat has not been discharged prematurely by an easterly burst; the ocean is delivering its energy to the surface cleanly, sustaining the climb toward the peak.

atmosphere.desc: SOI and trade winds confirm atmosphere–ocean coupling. Strong coupling is now confirmed present, not projected.
atmosphere.inference: Coupling is now strong and self-reinforcing — NOAA cites it explicitly as a source of very high confidence that El Niño continues through early 2027. The July SOI printed near −2.4 (about two standard deviations), trade winds have weakened substantially, and deep convection has locked into the central and eastern Pacific with suppression over Indonesia. MEI.v2 reached +2.41 for June–July — the highest value for that season in the record back to 1979. The Bjerknes feedback is fully engaged: this is the signature of a mature, intensifying event, and it removes any remaining possibility of a 2023-style decoupling.

regime.name: ENSO Regime Score
regime.interp: Very strong and record-class. Niño 3.4 at +2.6°C weekly, intensifying toward a peak NOAA now gives a 69% chance of exceeding every event since 1950.

coupling.name: Atmospheric Coupling
coupling.interp: Strong and self-reinforcing. NOAA cites the ocean–atmosphere coupling as a source of very high confidence in continuation through early 2027.
